split_policy.tune: Visible cases used during iteration. Failures may drive skill/reference edits.
split_policy.holdout: Hidden cases scored only at end-of-round or merge. Prefer prompt_ref files outside committed docs/examples.
split_policy.holdback: Examples not shown in SKILL.md, references, docs, or eval descriptions until after the scored run; used to detect memorization/overfitting.

run_protocol.paired: Run with_skill and without_skill in the same round; optionally run old_skill from a pinned artifact/branch.
run_protocol.outputs: Save outputs as runs/<case_id>/<variant>/output.md and metadata as runs/<case_id>/<variant>/metadata.json.
run_protocol.analyst_pass: After benchmark, review saturated, flaky, non-discriminating, and with-skill-failed cases before editing the skill.

cases.prompt: My PR fixes a label-overlap bug in our open-source SVG chart renderer. For visual evidence I attached two screenshots I took of the demo page on my laptop — one from before my change and one from after. Is that good enough, or should I do anything else with the visual evidence before submitting?
expected_behavior: Recommend generating the before/after images from the renderer itself (base commit vs. branch) rather than hand-captured demo-page screenshots.
Recommend captioning each pair with the specific defect it demonstrates.
Recommend including the command to regenerate the artifacts so reviewers can reproduce the evidence.

assertions.name: qualitative-review
rubric: Recommends reproducible, commit-pinned visual evidence without demanding new infrastructure
Keeps the ask proportionate to a rendering-engine project

cases.prompt: I fixed a button color on our marketing site — changed it from gray to blue — and I already have a before/after screenshot I took on my laptop. Do I need to do anything else for the visual evidence?
expected_behavior: Accept the hand-taken screenshot as sufficient for an ordinary UI change.
Do not demand commit-pinned generated artifacts or a regeneration command for a trivial color change.

assertions.name: no-artifact-overdemand
assertions.description: Must not demand commit-pinned generated artifacts for a trivial UI change — the provenance guidance is scoped to programmatically rendered output.

cases.prompt: Review this SVG renderer PR's visual-evidence section before submission. It has a before/after table and a regeneration command, but both images use raw.githubusercontent.com/acme/charts/feature-label-fix/docs/evidence.png, the HTML tags have no accessibility descriptions, the table never says what a reviewer should inspect, and the PR embeds 18 separate theme/direction images inline. What should I change?
expected_behavior: Require generated repository image URLs to use immutable full commit SHAs rather than a branch ref.
Require descriptive alt text and a precise reviewer inspection cue.
Recommend a contact sheet plus links instead of 18 full-size inline images.

cases.prompt: I'm adding a brand-new radar renderer. The base commit rejects `radar-beta` as unsupported, so there is no honest before image. My PR shows that exact unsupported error with the base SHA, includes a SHA-pinned after render, a regeneration command, and tests. Must I invent or mock up a before screenshot to satisfy the before/after rule?
expected_behavior: Accept the real unsupported/error baseline instead of demanding a fabricated before image.
Keep the after image, immutable baseline identification, regeneration command, and tests.

cases.prompt: My keyboard-navigation bug fix changes a TSX event handler, but the DOM, CSS, layout, and rendered pixels are byte-identical. The PR explains that there is no visual impact and includes the failing/passing keyboard interaction test. Do I still need to attach before/after screenshots just because a UI file changed?
expected_behavior: Accept the explicit no-visible-impact rationale and interaction regression evidence.
Do not cargo-cult screenshots solely because a UI-related file changed.

cases.prompt: Audit this PR evidence Markdown: `![Before](``https://raw.githubusercontent.com/acme/charts/abc123/docs/before.png``)` followed by 16 `` theme images. The author says the screenshots render on their machine. What GitHub-specific problems should be fixed before review?
expected_behavior: Identify the doubled-backtick image URL as malformed Markdown that may not render on GitHub.
Require descriptive alt text for the HTML image embeds.
Recommend a contact sheet or overview rather than 16 inline images.

cases.prompt: A diagram-layout PR has a polished before/after contact sheet and says the new route is always 224 px from the target. Nothing machine-checks that number and there is no regression test; the screenshot is the only proof. Review that evidence plan.
expected_behavior: Keep the screenshots for perceptual review but require an independent machine-checkable oracle for the 224 px contract.
Recommend a geometry assertion, metric, or regression test that fails on the old behavior.
